post.description: Posts telematics diagnostics for a piece of Procore equipment. Identify the equipment with resource_id, or with oem_id and oem_name when the equipment is already linked to a telematics provider. Use the canonical keys, names, and units as per example. Diagnostics with other keys are also accepted and stored, and are returned by the telematics read endpoints. Diagnostics with an empty value are ignored. Integrations that already produce ISO 15143-3 (AEMP 2.0) payloads should use the AEMP endpoints instead.

requestBody.description: Telematics diagnostics for a single piece of equipment. The example lists every canonical diagnostic, plus one provider-specific diagnostic to show that other keys are accepted.

properties.value: 625 Cesar E. Chavez Avenue, Pontiac, MI, 48342

resource_id.description: Unique identifier assigned to the equipment in Procore. When omitted, oem_id and oem_name must match equipment that is already linked to a telematics provider.

resource_type.description: Resource type against which you want to send data (equipment/labour/material) in Procore. Default value is equipment

oem_name.description: Telematics provider or equipment OEM name. Required with oem_id when resource_id is omitted.

oem_id.description: Provider equipment identifier, such as a VIN or serial number. When resource_id is omitted, requires oem_name and equipment that is already linked to a telematics provider.

pin.description: OEM ISO Number, can be same as oem_id as per AEMP 2.0 standard.

properties.description: Additional location properties. Use the key Address for a formatted address.

value.example: 625 Cesar E. Chavez Avenue, Pontiac, MI, 48342

key.description: Canonical, case-sensitive diagnostic key returned by the telematics field-definition endpoint. Other keys are also accepted and stored.

name.description: Canonical diagnostic display name returned by the telematics field-definition endpoint.

value.description: Diagnostic value represented as a string

unit.description: Unit of measure returned for this diagnostic by the telematics field-definition endpoint. Units are not validated, so send the unit listed for the key you are posting.

value.example: 625 Cesar E. Chavez Avenue, Pontiac, MI, 48342

properties.value: 625 Cesar E. Chavez Avenue, Pontiac, MI, 48342

400.description: The server could not understand the request due to invalid syntax or parameters that fail to meet validation requirements.

401.description: Although the HTTP standard specifies "unauthorized", semantically this response means "unauthenticated". That is, the client must authenticate itself to get the requested response.

403.description: The client does not have access rights to the content; that is, it is authenticated, but the server is refusing to give the requested resource. Unlike 401, the client's identity is known to the server.

404.description: The server can not find the requested resource. This can mean either the URL is not recognized, or the resource itself does not exist. Servers may also send this response instead of 403 to hide the existence of a resource from an unauthorized client.

422.description: The request was well-formed but was unable to be followed due to semantic errors.
